amendments.rule: A target head is the cross-language lexical display anchor: the English token that most directly realizes the source head's lexeme, with English syntax used only to break a genuine tie. Choose the lexical predicate over subjects and auxiliaries (`was gathered` heads on `gathered`), the noun in `of + noun`, and the substantive over a generic English noun supplied to expand it (`living creature` for a substantival adjective heads on `living`; rule 31 gives the test and governs the whole family). Where one morpheme is rendered by a multi-word English preposition, the head is the token carrying the lexeme rather than the connective: `מִן` → *out of* heads on *out*. **Where the ASV recasts one morpheme's relation as a fixed English phrase in which no word realizes that morpheme's own lexeme, head on the content word the phrase turns on, found by rule 31's subtraction test, and never on one of its connectives**: `מִן` → *of one piece with* heads on *piece*, because dropping *piece* leaves the phrase saying nothing while *of*, *one* and *with* are what English spends on the relation, exactly as `מִן` → *by reason of* heads on *reason*. This reaches only a rendering that drops the lexeme; where a word does realize it, the preceding sentence governs and the head stays there. Review this choice independently of the unit's edges.
amendments.why: Rule 24's multi-word clause tells you to head on "the token carrying the lexeme", which answers nothing when the ASV's rendering carries no such token. EXO.37 met that case seven times in מִן → *of one piece with* (37.8, 37.17, 37.21 three times, 37.22, 37.25), where no English word says *from* and the chapter had to reach for the phrase's content word. The corpus already heads such renderings on the content word rather than the connective — מִן → *by reason of* heads on *reason* in 17 units, → *some of* on *some* in 14, → *because of* on *because* in 32 — so the widening records what the finished chapters do instead of leaving the next pass to rediscover it or to head such an idiom on its *of*. The added sentence is a qualification of rule 24's own multi-word clause, so it belongs in that rule rather than as a new one pointing back at it.

conventions: מִן rendered by the fixed English phrase *of one piece with* (37.8, 37.17, 37.21 three times, 37.22, 37.25) is one unit on the preposition under rule 30, headed on *piece*. What follows keeps its own English: the article and noun of *with the mercy seat* in 37.8, and the suffix's own *it* in the suffixed clauses. No part of the four-word phrase is `added`, and none of it moves onto the noun or suffix beside it.

In the dimension formulas (37.1, 37.6, 37.10, 37.25) the clause's copula — written or italic *was* — joins the measure predicate's head noun אַמָּה and not the trailing חֲצִי it happens to stand beside, so the unit runs discontinuously across *and a half* under rule 25. Every measurement clause in the chapter is aligned this way; the competing reading, which attaches *was* to *half* because that is the word it follows, is named in the verse notes and was not taken.

זָהָב naming the material takes whatever function word the ASV spends on it and keeps it: *with* after צִפָּה (37.2, 37.4, 37.11, 37.15, 37.26, 37.28), *of* where it stands after the artifact noun (37.2, 37.6, 37.7, 37.13, 37.16, 37.17, 37.22, 37.23, 37.24, 37.26), and *golden* alone where the ASV renders it attributively (37.12, 37.27). MACULA's construct-versus-absolute tag on the artifact noun does not move that word — זֵר זָהָב with זֵר absolute (37.2, 37.26) and construct (37.12) place it identically — so cite rule 19 or rule 33 as the morphology warrants, but do not let the tag change the edge or the head, which is *gold* or *golden* throughout.

report: Read all 29 verses end to end against the 37-lemma candidate table and found no construction analysed two ways without something in the source licensing the difference. Every multi-treatment bucket resolves to the ASV writing different English over the same morphology.

The four biggest buckets check out: וְ is always the connective the ASV wrote (and / even / with); הוּא suffixes take whatever pronoun is written (thereof / of it / its / it), split into rectum-of plus pronoun under rule 19 wherever the ASV writes of; הַ is aligned where a the is written and unrepresented where none is (37.19, 37.21); עָשָׂה carries the subject pronoun only where the ASV repeats it.

Article placement is consistent under rules 29 and 47 across all 45 occurrences. Where an article morpheme stands it takes the written the (the four corners 37.13, the six branches 37.19/21, the altar of incense 37.25, the holy anointing oil 37.29 by fronting); where none stands the supplied the goes to the head of the nominal expression — the construct numeral where a construct heads the chain (the four feet 37.3/37.13, the two ribs 37.27, the two ends 37.8), the noun where the numeral is attributive (the one end 37.8, the other branch 37.19).

מִן is consistent too: of one piece with in the seven idiom clauses, out of in 37.18/19/21 with the participle keeping only going, at in 37.7/37.8, within and without fused in 37.2. The 37.18 division (there were going on the participle, out of on the preposition) is the same as 37.19 and 37.21, fixed by the two prepositions that have no participle beside them.

The three added units are each forced and none has a licensing morpheme in its clause: their in 37.9 (כְנָפַיִם is written bare, no suffix and no article), thereof in 37.16 (הַקְּשָׂוֺת carries no suffix, unlike the three preceding items), even in 37.17 (the clause's one אֵת stands on הַמְּנֹרָה, which the ASV renders bare — rule 16's explicit limit). Contrast 37.3, where a waw is present and takes its own even. No verse folds a comparable supplied word into a neighbouring morpheme, so the added-blind table hides no split.

BSB disagreements are both documented convention differences and neither is an error. The six To cases (37.4, 11, 15, 24, 26, 28) are rule 16's ruling that אֹתוֹ/אֹתָם splits into an unrepresented marker plus the suffix's pronoun; BSB counts the marker represented. The five Td cases (37.19, 37.21) are articles for which the ASV writes no the at all — in one branch, under two branches — which rule 29 requires be marked unrepresented. Nothing was changed to move the aggregate.

Recorded three conventions (the of one piece with idiom, the measurement copula, and the material זָהָב) and one amendment widening rule 24 to cover a head where the English rendering drops the source lexeme.
